The complex proposition fallacy involves
Option A: including more than one claim in the proposition and treating proof for one claim as proof for all the claims.
Option B: asking a question that includes either an unproven assumption or more than one question, thus making a straightforward yes or no answer meaningless.
Option C: arguing that a claim must be true because there is no evidence that it is false.
Option D: arguing something is inferior just because it doesn't do something it was never intended to do.
